column1: # Real standardebooks.org book pages, unedited, and each book's table of
# The book pages were fetched directly from the site, one request every 2s,
# in a seeded shuffle of its sitemap: 402 entries tried, 135 accepted as
# books. The check is the page's own og:type, "book". The sitemap also lists
# books the site has not made yet, at a placeholder whose og:type is
# "website" ("We don't have this ebook in our catalog yet", or a date the
# book enters the public domain); 266 answered with one, and one with a 404.
# Not through the dev Worker: the
# site's server refuses any request carrying X-Forwarded-For or
# CF-Connecting-IP, which a Worker always sends.
# The table-of-contents pages (listing column) were NOT fetched. robots.txt
# asks AI agents to stay off /ebooks/*/text*, so each was rebuilt instead
# from the book's source at the commit its book page names as deployed, by
# the site's own deploy transform: the verbatim XHTML step of
# inject-chapter-navigation-footer. Checked against the one table of
# contents fetched from the site (Moby Dick): byte for byte identical.
# Mixed on purpose: 1 entry to 387, novels, short fiction, poetry, plays and
# essays, 28 of them translations at a three-segment url.
# The columns after them were measured by a separate bs4/lxml script, NOT
# this app's parser, so the tests cross-check rather than echo it:
#   completed  always true — the site carries only finished books.
#   chapters   distinct files the table of contents (nav#toc) links, the
#              fragment dropped, leaving out the edition's furniture:
#              titlepage, halftitlepage, imprint, colophon, uncopyright, loi,
#   max_page   1 — no table of contents is split over pages.
#   listing    the table-of-contents capture the chapters are read from.
